title: Precision compression compatibility and stability action items
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: On 2026-02-17 we observed a class of incidents affecting several quantized serving variants that manifested as: (a) sudden accuracy drift on a subset of RLHF models for short-context prompts, (b) operator compatibility failures producing immediate worker crash-loops on Ampere GPUs, and (c) silent degradation where fallback to FP/compatible kernels did not trigger. The combined effect produced errors for ~3% of requests to a small set of enterprise customers and elevated tail latency while autoscaling attempted to recover. This ticket captures the post-incident analysis, short-term mitigations already applied, and a prioritized set of engineering action items to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-02-17 03:14 UTC — Pager alert: elevated 5xx rate for model-rw-emb-v2 quant-int8 pool detected by per-model error rate rule.
2026-02-17 03:22 UTC — Initial triage: spikes correlated with quantized pool and a subset of requests with long prefix KV cache hits.
2026-02-17 03:45 UTC — Hotpatch deployed: restrict canary traffic to FP32 variant for affected model family; rollback of latest kernel fuse commit to stop crash loops.
2026-02-17 04:10 UTC — Mitigation: onboarded an emergency rule to force fallback to verified kernels when dequant scale variance exceeds threshold.
2026-02-17 06:00 UTC — Incident declared resolved for majority of customers; follow-up investigation opened.
2026-02-20 10:00 UTC — Root cause hypothesis finalized after reproducer runs and kernel instrumentation.
2026-03-03 16:30 UTC — Hotpatch candidate PR merged to add stricter op-matching and fallback triggers; small canary run started.
2026-03-10 09:00 UTC — Canary expanded to dedicated pool and initial regression tests passed; preparing broader rollout in runtime-1.22.
2026-03-12 14:00 UTC — Current: monitoring baseline and additional test infra in progress; remaining action items listed below.
root_cause: A combination of two issues: (1) a regression in the quant-dequant kernel reorder where scale application order changed after an operator fusion optimization, producing numerical drift in low-scaling tokens that caused measurable accuracy regressions for certain RLHF prompts; and (2) an incomplete operator compatibility table in the compiler that allowed unsupported fused ops to be scheduled on Ampere kernels, causing deallocation races and crash-loops. Fallback logic existed but the trigger thresholds for 'scale variance' and 'op-mismatch' were too permissive, so some workers never tripped the fallback path.
impact_summary: Approximately 3% of requests for the affected model family saw either incorrect outputs (accuracy drift) or transient 5xx/worker restarts during the window. No customer data was exfiltrated. Several high-visibility enterprise customers experienced degraded SLA adherence for a 2-4 hour window during peak traffic.
actions: A1 — Add strict scale-consistency assertions to quant-dequant kernels and publish kernel contract tests (owner: Mateo) — due 2026-03-20.
A2 — Expand operator compatibility matrix in the compiler and add CI gate that rejects fused op schedules lacking verified kernel implementations (owner: Kernel team) — due 2026-03-12 (in progress).
A3 — Tighten fallback trigger thresholds: introduce explicit 'scale-variance' metric and a per-request fallback counter to avoid silent non-fallbacks (owner: Serving runtime) — due 2026-03-15.

A4 — Create a canary expansion plan that includes (i) short deterministic evals using RLHF prompt set, (ii) perf/cost baselines, (iii) per-region evening ramp schedule (owner: SRE + QE) — due 2026-03-18.
A5 — Add new observability dashboards for quantized path: token-distribution heatmaps, dequant-scale drift, per-op failure rates (owner: Console) — due 2026-03-22.
A6 — Update runbook: explicit recovery steps for quant kernel crashloops including immediate pool isolation and forced fallback to FP variants (owner: Incident Response) — due 2026-03-08 (completed).

A7 — Post-deploy quality gates: require zero-regression on our RLHF prompt set and a synthetic user-agent fuzz run before any quantized kernel gets pushed to production (owner: QE + RE) — due 2026-03-25.
A8 — Backfill canary tests for model families that were missing short prompt coverage; add automated monthly re-eval for critical families (owner: Model Onboarding) — due 2026-04-01.
A9 — Perform a small audit of deployed quant profiles for mismatched precision settings and correct any profiles with unsafe flags (owner: Runtime Config) — due 2026-03-14.
A10 — Customer communications: prepare a post-incident brief and targeted notices for impacted customers (owner: Customer Success & Legal) — due 2026-03-13 (in progress).
current_status_notes: Completed: emergency hotpatch to isolate FP variants, rollback of the problematic fuse commit in canary, runbook updates. In progress: kernel contract tests (A1), compiler matrix CI (A2), and canary expansion (A4). Blockers: one remaining fused-op implementation for Ampere that needs validation and a shortage of QE cycles for parallel canary lanes (mitigated by shifting 2 SRE engineers for 1 sprint).
follow_up_tasks: F1 — QE to author reproducible testcases that expose the scale-ordering drift and add them to nightly CI (owner: Priya S.) — due 2026-03-12.
F2 — Kernel team to instrument mem-safety checks to detect deallocation races earlier (owner: Viktor K.) — due 2026-03-18.
F3 — Runtime team to implement per-request telemetry tag for quant-fallback reason codes and expose to Console (owner: Mateo) — due 2026-03-20.
F4 — Product to review and approve expanded canary criteria and sign-off on rollout plan (owner: Lina R.) — due 2026-03-16.
F5 — Security to confirm no privileged surface was introduced by the temporary hotpatches (owner: Security) — due 2026-03-14 (completed).
F6 — Ops to run a dry-run of the pool-isolation playbook during maintenance window to validate operational latency impact (owner: SRE) — due 2026-03-19.
F7 — Create a short engineering postmortem doc for internal distribution that summarizes technical root causes, timeline, and decisions (owner: Asha Patel) — due 2026-03-13 (drafted).
F8 — Evaluate adding a guarded 'graceful-degrade' mode that reduces sequence length and enforces stricter cache warming for quantized pools under high variance (owner: Research) — due 2026-04-05.

F9 — Identify customers who saw the highest error delta and schedule follow-up calls to review mitigations and offer compensation if warranted (owner: Customer Success) — due 2026-03-14 (in progress).
